chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said: When water reaches the measure of two qullas, nothing makes it impure. And two qullas are two jars.

The first issue with this narration is that it is mursal. It is also possible that it was issued under taqiyya, for it is the position of many of the 'amma [Sunni scholars]. And even if we accept it, it is possible that the interpretation is what we mentioned in the preceding narration — namely, that the measure of two qullas equals the measure of a kurr, since that is not objectionable, for qulla in the [Arabic] language is the large jar. And on this basis, there is no contradiction between the narrations.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyya — precautionary dissimulation; a statement made to conform outwardly to the dominant view under duress
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: al-'amma — the Sunni community/scholars, distinguished from the Shia in classical Imami jurisprudential texts
key_terms.الْكُرِّ: kurr — the Shia jurisprudential standard water volume (~384 litres) above which water resists ritual impurity
key_terms.قُلَّتَيْنِ: two qullas — a traditional measure of water used in Sunni fiqh discussions on ritual purity
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: mursal — a hadith whose chain of narrators contains a gap or unnamed link

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia jurisprudential ruling on the two-qulla water threshold and how does Sheikh al-Tusi reconcile it with the kurr standard in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: Sheikh al-Tusi cites a hadith through a mursal chain — ending with an unnamed intermediary — from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), stating that water measuring two qullas (two large jars) cannot be made impure by anything. He then subjects it to threefold critique: the chain is broken (mursal); it may have been uttered under taqiyya since the two-qulla threshold was the position of many Sunni scholars; and even if accepted, two qullas can be equated to the Shia jurisprudential standard of a kurr, thereby reconciling it with all other narrations on the topic.
